title: Pride and Prejudice
subtitle: A chaotic duo found in chaotic minds.

content.text: Be ever so careful, dear. The fiery thirst for knowledge is blazing bright within you; be careful not to put it out.
Once, many fire thieves sat here, sipping coffee, as they tried to decipher the best angle to hold up their reeds to jam the burning wheel of Helios and steal his flame.
The gods are selfish. They're stingy with their might.
Shouldn't the gods be more generous?

branch.text: That's easy to say when the power's not yours to give. Knowing how to share is a rare virtue. Knowing how to share knowledge is a rarer virtue still.
"How can we transfer our wisdom into mortal minds?" The gods pondered.
Can inspiration be duplicated from one brain to another? It comes and goes like a gust of wind, so what can be done?
True. I'm sure the early customers of the bakery share the same philosophy.
The line must be respected, however hungry the latecomers may be.
There are many fire thieves in the field of science—many more than the bread buyers in the bakery. Take a look at these geeks in uniforms made of aerospace materials.
Among them are arcanists in love with science who spend most of their time studying diodes and machines, and humans who are passionate about the future, always finding new inspirations ...
Elements, lightning, atoms ... Perhaps you've forgotten their counterparts in arcanum, but you must be familiar with them as scientific discoveries.

These discoveries are the milestones of progress, sweetheart. The fire thieves firmly believed that they would be able to bring about many more technical revolutions: the fourth, the fifth, the 65535th ...
Sounds like a twist to the story is coming.
Not yet, darling. We've only finished the prologue. However, there is a "but" waiting down the road.
A sudden rain dampened people's enthusiasm for the future. The floppy disks and many clever minds perished in it.
Some of the fire thieves grieved the loss. They screamed and swore to retrieve what was lost.
What about the rest of them?
They returned to primitive chaos, like coelacanths crawling back into the ocean after thousands of years of evolution. Once again, they became the proteges of arcanum.
Perhaps they made the right choice by leaving that useless science behind. Who knows?
The story of the fire thieves has only gone this far, darling. At this point, no one knows what will happen to Prometheus or what's inside Pandora's box.

content.text: Some will receive it. First come, first served.

trails.title: Equipment Failure Repair Record
trails.description: A nifty little fellow, the crystallization of tangible wisdom.

content.text:
Conway Automaton V, also known as LifeGame V. It is the most popular mind expansion tool in Laplace, capable of simulating cell life and death calculations within a maximum of 2^16 pixels with predefined rules, and supporting modular assembly and custom interfaces, among other features. It has been proven to maintain the mental agility of researchers and can simulate most current popular games.

    Almost all Conway Automatons were lost in the "Storm" or scrapped to make room for important instruments—this is the last remaining one in the Scientific Computing Center. Although the Conway Automaton V cannot play a practical role in password decryption, to ensure the enthusiasm of the decryption team's work, an urgent repair request is hereby made.

    If the repairs cannot be completed in a short period of time, it is hoped that a substitute can be allowed during the repair period, such as the latest handheld console, the Game Dude Color.

items.text: Pride and Prejudice
Office of Director, Laplace
An unknown incantation.
A mask that has proven to be extremely dangerous.
These are the only leads they currently have on the "Storm."
Her metallic fingers pick up another stack of files.
These are the test results of the Manus mask, confirming the presence of asymmetrical nuclide R.
The robot studies them carefully. The slit on her face pulses in contemplation.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: What is the status of the sampling, Simone? Any updates from the Timekeeper?

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: For the moment, no. The people on the island are still suspicious of the Foundation's motives, so she hasn't had a second chance to collect any samples.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: But she has called in an hour ago. We were informed that she will return to the cave shortly.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: She also warned us that the immunity zone on the island appears to be shrinking. The safe zone is not stable.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hm.
The robot did not put on a face today. Simone can only read her mood from the narrow slit.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: Ma'am, have you noticed something?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: They are unrelated, Simone.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The mask and the incantation are indeed related to Manus Vindictae, but they are unrelated to each other.
She moves the sealed Manus mask aside.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: If the account of the Vienna investigator is correct, one cannot help but question:

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Why would Arcana not simply give the masks to Isolde and her brother?

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: Investigator Marcus's report was highly lacking, making it challenging for us to infer what truly happened.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I suppose we can be skeptical that the report is incomplete. But it is all we have for now.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: She did a good job. I could not have asked for more.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We all heard it. "An ancient miracle, a circle of salvation."
The robot extends her hand, drawing an imaginary circle in the air.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The leader of Manus Vindictae promised a miracle, but the mask is far from it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The mask is a tool of control, designed to identify and enslave the believers. Matthew has demonstrated its effects for us.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But this ritual is different.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: Do you mean the ritual is more sophisticated than the mask?
The robot nods approvingly.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Perhaps, but it is not entirely definitive.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The investigators in Vienna completed their mission spectacularly, and now Matthew has proven that the mask is useless for our purposes. Its immunity was only a cover for its other functions.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And the mask has powerful and irreversible side effects. Even if we find out how it protects the wearer from the "Storm," we cannot use it on our colleagues.
She picks up the scrip.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: If this incantation is verified to be true,

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: it will be our Promethean fire.
Cryptography Team's Office

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: This ritual is useless to us.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Save yourself the trouble. We're not getting anywhere with this.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: What?
The room is cluttered with all sorts of sophisticated equipment.
The floor is littered with scrap paper. The researchers haven't lifted their heads or taken a break for quite some time.
The cryptography lead stares at Enigma, a fresh cup of coffee in his hand. His patience is wearing thin as the metaphorical string labeled "tolerance" in his mind is finally about to snap.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Explain yourself, Adler. What do you mean the ritual is useless?

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: You barely sat down! My coffee's still hot!
The cryptographer solemnly hands the lead a stack of papers from his desk.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I don't need to waste any more time. It's simple logic.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The current information is insufficient for cryptographic decryption. We're attempting an exhaustive brute force, comparing every ancient text and record to find the language or corresponding text. It's like looking for a needle in a colossal haystack.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Even if we stumble onto a match, none of us can validate such a thing. A breakthrough in this regard is simply not possible—

items.speaker: Researcher II
items.text: You can't be serious.
Across the room, a man stands up abruptly from his chair, clenching a pen in his hand.

items.speaker: Researcher II
items.text: And what is the basis of your reasoning? Have you figured out the mechanics behind the ritual?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I didn't need to understand the intricacies of arcanum to deduce this. It was simple log- ...

items.speaker: Researcher II
items.text: So you never even tried to understand it. With your supposedly superior human reasoning, you dismissed all of our dedication and hard work, just like that.

items.speaker: Researcher II
items.text: Who the f*** do you think you are!?
Before anyone can react, the researcher lunges at Enigma and punches him right in the face.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Wh—?
Enigma brings a hand up to his cheek, looking more confused than angry.

items.speaker: Researcher II
items.text: Matthew was right. You arrogant fools, clueless morons!

items.speaker: Researcher II
items.text: Get out of my face, you humanocentric narcissist. Go to hell!
The researcher snarls, brandishing his pen like a soldier brandishing a dagger.
Much to his frustration, his swing loses power mid-air—another casualty of the neck and shoulder pain that plagues this office.
Enigma narrowly avoids the attack, bewildered by the turn of events.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Was this really necessary? I was just sharing my conclusion.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Ugh, it was the mask! I should've thought of that. He worked in the same lab as Matthew, and he must've been exposed to the mask.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But his physical exam seemed fine. Is there an incubation period!?

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Does he seem fine to you now? Huh?

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: No, Williams, put that down! That's the only Conway Automaton V left after the "Storm"!
He is met with a guttural growl, followed by the deafening crash of metal against wall.
The machine whizzes past his head and shatters to pieces on impact.
The cryptography lead can feel his sanity teetering on the brink. He staggers towards the door, frantically smacking the big red button on the wall.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Security! Security! We've got a code red!!!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: So, what are the implications for the decryption?

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: There were no unintended consequences. We were able to control Williams in time, and the Conway Automaton V he destroyed wasn't useful to our work anyway.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I am glad you kept the damages to a minimum.
Lucy turns off the screen in front of her and turns around.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Since you are still here, Mr. Ulrich, I take it as a sign that you have more to report?
In a secluded area of the hallway, an emotionally charged complaint is about to take place.
The cryptography lead tries to keep his voice low, looking completely disheveled from the turmoil he has just endured.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Williams was merely an accident, ma'am, but Adler is a loose cannon on the team. We need to talk about this.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: With all due respect, I still don't understand why you put him on the team.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: He may have made his contributions to Laplace, but that was eight years ago. Now he's just an irritating defeatist and a staunch supporter of humanocentrism.
Every particle of ferrofluid in his helmet is vibrating with rage, his voice rising involuntarily.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: He never understood the arcanum, or tried. He's still stuck in the time before the first "Storm" and refuses to acknowledge that his small, beautiful world is gone!

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: How can someone like that help us?
The robot senses his doubt and frustration—there may be more sentiments and underlying issues at play. She pauses for a moment before answering, as if deep in thought.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I understand your concern, but I have not heard anything about the incapacitation of Adler Hofmann.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Incapaci—What? He got a few scratches at most. The guy barely touched him.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: So he is fine. I am glad we agree. Is there anything else you would like to report?
The robot waits 5 seconds for an answer. But there isn't one.
This must be the social cue that it is her turn to speak.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: His lack of knowledge on arcanum is exactly why we need him. His human perspective will offer valuable insights on arcane rituals.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The results of this study will not only be used to save arcanists,

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: but also humans who share the same world with us.
The cryptography lead tries to argue further, but Lucy is certain the issue has been sufficiently addressed.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We are racing against the clock, mister, and your report on personal disputes and racial conflicts has wasted 2 minutes and 37 seconds of our time.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: If he refuses to cooperate, you have every right to remove him from the team. That is your responsibility.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Oh.
From the other end of the corridor, the subject of their argument approaches, looking deeply upset and clutching a stack of papers.
Clearly, he has heard every word they just said.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I am relieved that you survived your altercation.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: What would you like to report?
Their eyes meet, making both of them squirm uncomfortably. This is undoubtedly one of the most awkward moments in both of their careers.
After a prolonged silence, Ulrich steps back and walks away.
Without even looking back at him, Enigma begins his report in a low voice.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'm fed up with wasting time, ma'am. The setback with the mask has already driven too many people insane.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: That's why you should take a look at this.
He hands the stack of files to Lucy.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I can logically deduce that our current direction is another dead end. The incantation isn't long enough for cryptographic decryption.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: We will have to turn to ancient records. Perhaps we'll find something in age-old manuscripts, in tablet inscriptions, or in the memories of powerful arcanists.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But even if we find it, we can't validate it because none of us can cast the skill.
The robot remains silent during his pessimistic remarks, flipping through each page of the file.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Low-ranking arcanists can't cast high-ranking skills, even if they know the exact pronunciation and meaning of the incantation.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Gnosis is beyond reason like that and cannot be debated. It stems from raw intuition rather than logic and intellect, is shaped by personal experiences and natural abilities, and cannot be intentionally replicated.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And the most determining factor—it relies on the arcanist's purity of blood.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The miracle ritual you hold such hopes for belongs to the leader of Manus Vindictae, a pure-blooded arcanist whose power is beyond our imagination.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: It's like asking a toddler to solve Goldbach's conjecture. It's completely beyond the boundaries of our limits!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But you are not an arcanist.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Why should you play by their rules?
The man is taken aback by her question. It's something he's never considered before.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You are right. Arcanists differ due to their purity of blood.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Researcher Medicine Pocket has already reported the linear correlation between the bloodline of an arcanist and their abilities, and has drawn a conclusion ten times more extreme.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Then you should listen. That's their area of expertise.
Her neck moves subtly, almost like shaking her head.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We know that our cryptographers do not have the power to validate the ritual.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And we do not expect you to do that. All I ask of you is to come up with a feasible plan, and to do it as a team.
Enigma turns away, repulsed at the mention of "team."
Lucy finishes reading the report and hands it back to him.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Your deduction is logical, but not practical or actionable.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: So I should return this to you.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: What?
The glow in her eye slit is strangely reassuring, almost like a smile.
She looks out of the window.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Your logic is impressive, Adler. But do not let it limit your thinking.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You spoke of the boundaries of arcane power, but logic has its limits too, no?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Knowledge can be obtained through various means, such as intuition, logical reasoning, empirical observations, and teachings from others.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Your team is not the only one cracking the ritual through their own means. If you fail, we will turn to the others. And if that approach is wrong, we will try another. If no solution is found before the "Storm," we will simply wait for the next one.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: What matters is we keep moving forward, no matter the cost. We must keep to the path, or we will be swept away like dust in the rain.
For once, the researcher does not argue.
He whispers, as if talking to himself.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: If one team fails, you can still turn to the others.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Then why? Why did it have to be Greta?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Forget it. Just a bitter, irrational thought.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: This marks the end of my efforts. Hopefully, "the others" will bring you the needed breakthroughs.
The man walks away in anger.
But after only a few steps, a question comes to mind.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You've been waiting here for a while. Are you expecting someone?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You aren't the type to waste time listening to us whine, so there must be something here worthy of your attention.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Is someone close to a breakthrough?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Nothing of the sort.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I am recharging. We have a public power outlet here.
She moves her joints as if standing for so long has stiffened her body.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But I am indeed waiting.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The doves of the White Stone House are here.
The sound of flapping wings fills the air.
The researcher is astonished as the creature, with a texture similar to plaster, perches on her metal finger.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Good.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Someone closer to the "limit" has given us aid.
TO BE CONTINUED…
